Synopsis:
You wake up the morning after the night where Astarion (companion) tried to bite you. Depending on your choices, he might have bitten you consensually or you might have told him to piss off. He'll be wary to see if you're still in a forgiving mood. The other companions chime in with their opinions on having a vampire around, and the player defends keeping Astarion in the party.

Cluster Contexts:
- CAMP_AstarionHungerC_CRD_Astarion_MorningAfter.json: You wake the morning after the night Astarion tried to bite you — depending on your previous choices he either did so with your consent or you told him to piss off. Astarion is a companion and a vampire spawn, so he'll be cautious this morning to gauge whether you're still forgiving or ready to punish him. Other companions may chime in with judgement or concern about having a vampire in the party, and some follow-up lines only appear once you or they learn more about Astarion. Off-screen background that matters: Astarion was enslaved to a master (Cazador) and bears carved scars from that past, and he’s been preoccupied with dark books and secrets that make him edgy.
- CAMP_AstarionHunger_SCO_Companion.json: You and Astarion are traveling as companions; in the night he reveals himself as a vampire by hunching over your bedroll to feed and is caught when you wake and fight him off. He reacts with alarm and pleading, insisting he rarely kills for food (feeding on animals) and begging for a small taste to restore his strength so he can continue helping you against the shared threat (the worms/tadpole). If you press him he grows defensive and bargains; if you consent he eagerly drinks, becomes invigorated, and turns cocky and overconfident. Other campmates or larger plot threads (Shadowheart, camp activities, temple/curse matters) may be happening nearby but are not part of this immediate bedside confrontation.
- END_GameFinale_ROM_RomanceFates_Astarion.json: You and Astarion are alone in a private inn bedroom the morning after an intimate night together, following the party’s confrontation with the Netherbrain and the events at Cazador’s palace. Off‑screen, the party has already dealt with Cazador’s ritual in some fashion, and Astarion’s personal fate there can vary: he may have killed Cazador and taken his power (becoming a Vampire Ascendant), killed Cazador but remained a vampire spawn (with possible reactivity if he also killed other spawn/prisoners), or left Cazador alive. Astarion has a fraught, prior relationship with Cazador and is known to the palace cultists, so references to being claimed, hunted, or treated as “one of their betters” reflect that history. The morning conversation therefore oscillates between fear and vulnerability, possessive anger if the player threatens to leave, or confident, predatory optimism if Astarion has just gained vampiric power.
- Astarion_InParty2_Nested_KilledYou.json: Astarion killed you during the camp night where he bit you.When you talk to him in the morning he tells you he was worried about you.
- Astarion_InParty2_Nested_BlackMassFollowUp.json: This scene plays out in camp just after the Black Mass ritual: Astarion has undergone a dramatic change (in some branches becoming a vampire lord) and — in the samples shown — either converted the player into a vampire spawn or offered to. Off‑screen the ritual involved violence and deaths the player may be struggling to reconcile, and Astarion now speaks from a place of new power and ambition (he name‑drops Mephistopheles’ blessings and imagines a “crimson palace” of spawn). He’s emotionally distant and inscrutable since the ritual, while the player is processing both the practical consequences (sunlight, new abilities) and the moral/relationship fallout. This exchange clarifies what happened that night and sets up choices about trust, romance, and how far the player will follow Astarion’s plans.

context: You wake the morning after Astarion tried to feed on you — depending on earlier choices he either got a small, consensual taste or you drove him off. Astarion is a vampire spawn and former slave of Cazador (marked by carved scars) and has been brooding over dark books and secrets, so he’ll be nervy and testing whether you’re still forgiving. Other companions in camp may react with judgment or concern about harboring a vampire, and some lines only unlock once you or they learn more about Astarion’s past. The player line “You’re lucky I didn’t kill you” signals anger and mistrust while also indicating you’ve chosen to keep him in the party despite that tension; exact emotional beats can vary with how the Cazador/Black Mass storyline played out.
